coverage: Fernandina: what the 2024 eruption did to plants and animals, whether visitor sites stayed open, and the size of the island and of its land iguana population
sample_note: All read 2026-11-18; none of the three pages shows a date. “Flujo de lava de la erupción del volcán La Cumbre llega al mar”: rangers at the Canal Bolívar base, west of Isabela, reported the lava at the sea after 35 days of activity; the flow down the southeast flank affected endemic vegetation (scalesia, palo santo, some cacti) and part of the land iguana’s habitat; marine iguanas, fish and coastal invertebrates could be affected at the sea entry; no people live on Fernandina; visitor sites stayed open. “Inicio de proceso eruptivo en el volcán La Cumbre”: start on Saturday 2 March 2024 at 23:50 Galápagos time; no settlements; no threat to tourism; eruptions are part of the islands’ natural cycle. “Población de iguanas amarillas de Galápagos aumentó en la isla Fernandina”: about 46,000 land iguanas from fieldwork in 2018 (capture, mark, recapture), published in Herpetology Notes; the island is the third largest, 638 km2.
notes: The releases carry no dates on the page; the sources list dates two of them by the events they describe (March and April 2024). The lava release says animals “could” be affected and reports no deaths; the page says exactly that.

coverage: El Chichón: the alert level and who sets it, what each level means, the restricted area, the earthquake count of summer 2025, the people and communities near the crater, the evacuation routes and shelters
sample_note: All read 2026-11-18. CNPC release of 18 Dec 2025 (read twice): the scientific advisory committee kept the Semáforo de Alerta Volcánica “sin cambios, en Amarillo, Fase 1”, to confirm whether the activity settles at a base level; Yellow Phase 1 described as new activity with seismicity above normal, new fumaroles, changes in temperature, gases or the water of the crater; nobody to enter the crater or go near it, a safety radius of at least one kilometre; 13 evacuation routes, six end points, 22 temporary shelters verified. Chiapas communiqué 065 (19 Aug 2025): 307 earthquakes from 1 June to 18 August 2025 within 20 km of the crater, magnitudes 1.4 to 3.4. Communiqué 067 (26 Aug 2025, read twice): a working group (CENAPRED, UNAM’s Instituto de Geofísica, UNICACH, the state, among others) analysed the change in the size of the lake, seismicity, ground deformation and gas emission: signs consistent with a modification of the hydrothermal system; monitoring to be strengthened with an eye on a possible reactivation of the magmatic system; crater access only for accredited researchers; the volcano is in the municipality of Chapultenango. Plan Operativo (PDF, 2025): the level is set by the CNPC; Yellow Phase 2 brings an exclusion radius of 2.5 km from the crater rim, Red 5 km and then 10 km; 3 localities with 207 people within 5 km and 24 communities with 5,565 people within 10 km; 70 km NNW of Tuxtla Gutiérrez and 77 km SSW of Villahermosa; crater 1 km wide and 300 m deep. Press list (proteccioncivil.chiapas.gob.mx/prensa): entries of 25 Aug 2026 (new instruments for Chichonal) and 8 Sep 2026 (volcano monitoring), titles only. Tabasco’s programme 2026 (PDF, first 200,000 of 237,227 characters): the central dome stood at 1,235 m before 1982; Teapa, Huimanguillo and Tacotalpa most exposed to ashfall; no level in force stated.
notes: The newest statement of the alert level that could be read is the release of 18 Dec 2025; the page gives the level with that date and says nothing newer was read. Chiapas’s communiqués 025 and 027 of 2026 are listed on its press page, but their own addresses were not opened (owner away: the reader may fetch only addresses that are search results), so the page cites only their titles. Also read, not cited: the CNPC release of 27 Aug 2025 (a slight increase in seismicity between 6 June and 21 August 2025; a command post), communiqués 068 and 070 (the command post in Chapultenango; “Fase 1” on 5 Sep 2025; a broadband station at Viejo Volcán) and Chiapas’s Programa Especial 2025 (magnitudes 1.4 to 3.6, depths 1 to 20 km). The Plan Operativo counts 32 shelters and the CNPC release 22 verified: the page prints the release’s figure with its date.
